note: Ahrefs competitor research across the ten primary markets that had none, exported so it survives the Advanced plan expiring on 8 October 2026. Seed target numbeo.com for every market, date 2026-09-01, mode subdomains, ordered by share. The seed is the same everywhere on purpose: the size of the common keyword set is then comparable across markets and is itself a measurement of how developed this cluster is in each one.
caveat: share is computed over the keywords a competitor shares with the seed. Where keywordsCommon is small the share figure is arithmetic rather than meaningful, and the market rows below carry commonKeywordsTop as the number that should be read instead.

tw.omitted: Five further rows returned by the API are general purpose properties with zero common keywords and no bearing on this cluster.

topPages.note: The strongest local site in each market where one exists, ordered by organic traffic, twenty rows each. The point is the page shape, not the traffic: these are the URL patterns that earn in a market Livdar has never entered.

combien-coute.net.shape: One page per commodity per country, plus one hub per commodity. Cost of living country pages exist but earn less than the single item pages.

rows.topKeyword: cout de la vie en suisse
cout de la vie en espagne
coût de la vie au maroc
ile maurice cout de la vie

auslandsguru.com.shape: One page per country on one question, cost of living, and nothing else in the top twenty. Domain rating seven, so the ranking is earned by the page rather than by the domain.

laenderdaten.info.shape: Ranked lists across all countries on one measure each, plus per country data pages. The ranking pages outearn the country pages by a wide margin, which is the same finding the United States research produced, in a second language.
laenderdaten.info.note: Two of its highest pages are anatomical statistics. They are recorded because they are in the data, not because Livdar would build them.

rows.topKeyword: welches land hat die meisten inseln

livingcost.org.shape: Country against the reader own country. Sixteen of the top twenty are /cost/{other}/united-kingdom or a United Kingdom region. The same site in the United States would rank a different set of URLs, which is what the audience axis means in practice.

custodevida.com.br.shape: Domestic city against domestic city. Nine of the top twenty are /comparar/{state-city}/{state-city}/ inside Brazil, and the rest are single Brazilian cities. No international comparison appears at all, which is the opposite of what a global taxonomy would have predicted for this market.

preciosmundi.com.shape: Country prices split by spending category, /{country}/precios-supermercado and /{country}/precio-restaurantes, plus a pair comparison path. Traffic is small in absolute terms, so this is evidence of shape rather than of size.

rows.topKeyword: cuanto cuesta una barra de pan en argentina
cuanto cuesta una cerveza en argentina

hikersbay.com.shape: One prices page per country with the market as a query parameter. Every Italian top keyword is a single item price question. The site is a translation layer over one dataset, which is exactly the thing the no identical translations rule forbids, and it still ranks, so the rule is about quality rather than about whether the shape can rank.
